title: Moss and Pip's Wobbly Path
markdown:
High up in the Starry Hills, where the air tasted like cool fresh mint and the stars looked close enough to tickle, lived a young goblin named Moss. Bright round eyes. A little pointed cap that wiggled when he walked, most when he was excited. His very best friend was a fluffy white rabbit called Pip. Long ears like little antennas. He sniffed for interesting smells. He looked for shiny pebbles.

One moonlit evening the moon hung like a slice of creamy cheese. “Come, Pip. Let us go into the Little Silver Forest. The moon is bright, and the path will be as clear as a robin’s song.”

Pip, nibbling a dandelion puff, thumped a hind leg and hopped beside him. Leaves shimmered like tiny mirrors. Tonight the forest seemed to be playing a special game.

“Moss,” Pip twitched his pink nose. “Doesn’t this path feel rather wiggly to you?”

It wove and looped. They wanted the Whispering Waterfall. They were going in a circle, passing the same plump glowing mushrooms for the third time.

“Oh dear.” Moss pulled out his map, made with great care, all the nooks of the Starry Hills. A big smudge covered the way to the waterfall. “This map is being a bit confused.”

Pip had found moss that glowed bright sapphire blue. He nudged it, charmed, and forgot the wiggly path.

“Let’s try to focus.” A gentle puzzle. The hills were full of little surprises.

A soft pretty humming. Around a silvery tree: a kindly witch, Willowyn, eyes twinkling like the brightest stars, sorting a basket—lavender like sweet dreams, mint of pure freshness, thyme of warm happy sunshine.

“Hello there, little ones. Are you lost?”

Moss, shy but hopeful. “We wanted to see the Whispering Waterfall. But the path keeps changing its mind.” He showed the smudge.

Tiny silver bells of a chuckle. “The path is guided by the big Mountain Lantern, high on the peak, to keep paths straight. Sometimes, when a map isn’t clear, it confuses the light. If the map is messy, the guidepost can point the wrong way.”

Moss looked at the smudge, then up at the faint glow.

Willowyn took the map. A delicate touch smoothed the ink, the intended path clear. “Now, if you can just guide that light a little more towards the falls, the path will straighten.”

He held it up. His finger pointed the lantern symbol toward the tinkling sound. Suddenly the real Mountain Lantern shone brighter and straighter, a clear silver beam. The path underfoot felt firm and true, no longer wobbly.

“Oh, thank you.” Pip hopped, ears perked.

They set off down the now-steady silver path, not a wiggle in sight, to the shimmering tinkling waterfall. After its happy song, the lantern’s unwavering glow led them home. Moss tucked the map away, a little more neatly. Pip curled beside him, dreaming of blue glowing moss. The cheese-slice moon hung where it had begun. All was well.
